title.en: How Do Your Notes Catch an Idea?
title.zh: 想法刚来时：你的笔记会怎么接？

description.en: Six note-play choices about a useful line, a quick visual sketch and connections between fragments. Find your way of catching a small idea on paper.
description.zh: 六次纸上记录选择，用一句有用话、快画图形或连接碎片，发现你会怎样接住小想法。

introduction.en: Imagine recording one recreational idea with paper you already have. You do not need neat handwriting or drawing experience. The result describes a note format you selected today, not memory, intelligence or a scientifically established learning style.
introduction.zh: 想象用已有纸记一个休闲想法，不需要字整齐或会画画。结果只描述今天选的笔记形式，不测记忆、智力，也不认定科学学习风格。

focus.en: Capturing an idea as a plain verbal cue, a visual relationship or a link between separate fragments.
focus.zh: 用一句话、一张示意图，或两个片段之间的一条联系，记住刚冒出的想法。

prompt.en: A small idea appears while you are making something. You…
prompt.zh: 做东西时冒一个小想法，你会……

label.en: Write one sentence saying what you want to return to.
Draw a rough shape showing how the parts relate.
label.zh: 粗画形状，显出部件关系。

label.en: Put two related fragments beside it with connecting marks.
label.zh: 旁边放两个相关碎片，画线相连。

prompt.en: You have only a little space on the page. You keep…
prompt.zh: 纸上只有一点空间，你留……

label.en: The simplest outline that makes the idea visible.
label.zh: 让想法可见的最简单轮廓。

label.en: The question or next step in ordinary words.
label.zh: 用普通话写问题或下一步。

label.en: The connection that made this fragment interesting.
label.zh: 让碎片有意思的那处联系。

prompt.en: You return to yesterday’s note. You most need…
prompt.zh: 回看昨天笔记，你最需要……

label.en: A line explaining why I wrote it.
A few visible links to the other parts of the idea.
label.zh: 与想法其他部分的几处可见连接。

label.en: A rough picture of the arrangement I had in mind.

prompt.en: A new fragment does not fit the first version. You…

label.en: Place it beside the old one and draw the possible relationship.
label.zh: 放在旧片旁，画可能关系。

label.en: Redraw a small variation rather than perfecting the first sketch.
label.zh: 重画小变化，不完善第一草图。

label.en: Write a short contrast between the two versions.

prompt.en: A willing friend asks what the note means. You show…
prompt.zh: 愿意的朋友问笔记什么意思，你展示……

label.en: The one sentence that gives it a starting point.
The part of the sketch that holds the main relationship.
label.zh: 草图里承载主要关系的部分。

label.en: The two fragments and why I connected them.
label.zh: 两个碎片，以及为什么相连。

prompt.en: What would make this little note useful later?
prompt.zh: 什么让小笔记以后仍有用？

label.en: The page reminds me what connected to what.
label.zh: 纸页提醒什么连着什么。

label.en: I can picture the idea without needing a polished drawing.
label.zh: 不用精致图，也能想象想法。

label.en: One ordinary line lets me begin again.
label.zh: 一句普通话就让我重新开始。

summary.en: Your note catches the idea in a line you can understand later. The point is not polished prose but a small return path. This portrait values plain words without suggesting they are the best format for every idea or every person.
summary.zh: 你用一句以后仍看得懂的话，把想法记下来。重点不在文笔，而在过一阵还能想起自己要做什么。这是你选的一种记录方式，不表示文字适合所有想法或所有人。

example.en: You might write “try the narrow paper strip as a handle” and leave the surrounding design unfinished until another visit.
example.zh: 你可以写下“试试用窄纸条做把手”，把还没想完的设计留到下次继续。

strength.en: A short verbal cue can preserve the reason for an idea and make it easier to take one wanted next step.
strength.zh: 一句简短的提示，能保留当时为什么有这个想法，也方便你以后接着试。

tradeoff.en: A sentence can flatten a visual relationship that a tiny drawing would show more directly. Adding a sketch remains available.
tradeoff.zh: 有些位置关系，画一笔比写一句更清楚。文字记不明白的地方，仍可以补一张小草图。

experiment.en: Write one note using the words you would naturally say aloud. Read it once later and add only the detail you actually needed.
experiment.zh: 用自己自然会说的话写一条笔记。稍后读一次，只添确实需要的细节。

summary.en: Your note holds the idea through a visible arrangement. A rough box, arrow or silhouette can be enough to bring the relationship back. The ending concerns a chosen note format rather than drawing talent or visual intelligence.
summary.zh: 你用大致的形状和位置记住想法。一个方框、一支箭头或一道轮廓，可能就足以让你以后想起来。这里说的是你选的笔记形式，不评画技，也不评所谓视觉智力。

example.en: You might sketch two paper pieces overlapping and add an arrow, instead of describing the whole construction in several paragraphs.
example.zh: 两片纸该怎样重叠，可以简单画出来，再加一支箭头，不必用几段文字解释整个结构。

strength.en: A small rough sketch can keep spatial relationships available and give a later trial something concrete to respond to.
strength.zh: 一张粗略的小图能保留空间关系，方便你下次照着尝试或调整。

tradeoff.en: A picture without any label may be hard to read after the moment has passed. One plain word can help without making the drawing elaborate.
tradeoff.zh: 没有任何标注的图，过一阵可能就看不懂了。补上一个关键的词即可，不必把草图画得很精细。

experiment.en: Sketch one idea in under a minute and add the single label that makes it understandable to your later self. Leave the rest rough.
experiment.zh: 用不到一分钟画下一个想法，再添一个能让以后自己看懂的标注，其余部分保持粗略就好。

summary.en: Your note keeps the relation between pieces, not only the pieces themselves. An arrow or short link can preserve why two fragments met. The portrait values a particular connection rather than claiming that more connected notes always mean better thinking.
summary.zh: 你不只记下几个零散片段，也会记下它们为什么有关。一支箭头或一句说明，就能留住当时的联系。这不意味着连线越多，思考就越好。

example.en: A line from a story and a small paper shape might sit on the same page with one note explaining the idea that linked them.
example.zh: 在同一页放上一句故事文字和一个纸片造型，再写一句话，说明它们怎样让你想到同一个点子。

strength.en: A visible connection can help you revisit the spark between two details without reconstructing the entire earlier chain of thought.
strength.zh: 保留一处明确的联系，以后就容易重新想起两个细节碰在一起的灵感，不必从头还原整段思路。

tradeoff.en: Too many links can make a small note hard to enter. One useful connection may matter more than a complete web.
tradeoff.zh: 连线太多，笔记反而不好读。一处真正有用的联系，可能比一张完整的关系网更值得留下。

experiment.en: Place two fragments from a harmless idea together and write why they connect. Keep only one link you would actually want to revisit.
experiment.zh: 把一个普通点子里的两个片段放在一起，写明它们为什么有关，只保留一条你以后还想回看的联系。

description.en: Catch a small idea with a plain line, a rough sketch or links between fragments. Six note-play choices lead to three portraits without labeling a fixed learning style.
description.zh: 用一句普通话、粗草图或碎片连线，接住小想法。六次纸上记录选择，读三种画像，不贴固定学习风格标签。

question.en: Does choosing sketches mean I am a visual learner?
question.zh: 偏选草图，就表示我是视觉学习者吗？

answer.en: No fixed learning style is inferred. A sketch can show an arrangement, a line can preserve a reason, and links can preserve a relationship. The quiz concerns the format you chose for this small note.
answer.zh: 不据此认定固定学习风格。草图可显排列，文字可留理由，连线可留关系。测试只谈为这条小笔记所选的记录形式。
